boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Elon rituals linking acorns, historic artifacts, weekly gatherings, ceremonies and campus celebrations to the university’s identity.

cards.title: Arrive With an Acorn, Leave With a Sapling
cards.subtitle: Elon bookends each student’s education with two pieces of an oak tree
cards.notes: Keep the acorn from New Student Convocation, then compare that opening symbol with the oak sapling presented near graduation.
cards.short_summary: New students receive an acorn; graduating students receive an oak sapling representing their growth.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon states that new students receive an acorn at the beginning of their college careers and each graduate receives an oak sapling; the sapling tradition became permanent in 1992.
cards.source_title: Symbols & Sayings | Elon Traditions | Elon University
cards.access_notes: The acorn and sapling presentations are tied to official new-student and graduating-student ceremonies.

cards.title: Touch the Bell That Survived Old Main
cards.subtitle: A 1923 fire survivor becomes part of the first-year procession
cards.notes: Look for the historic bell while passing through Alamance Building, and read its fire-survival story before touching it respectfully.
cards.short_summary: New students pass and touch the bell saved from Old Main during their Convocation procession.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon reports that new students process through Alamance Building past the bell that hung in Main Building before the building was destroyed by fire in 1923, and students touch the bell.
cards.source_title: New Student Convocation begins ‘powerful journey of questions and curiosity’ at Elon
cards.access_notes: The documented ceremonial touch occurs during the New Student Convocation procession through Alamance Building.

cards.title: Make Tuesday Morning College Coffee
cards.subtitle: A class-free gathering has connected Elon’s campus since 1984
cards.notes: Build a Tuesday pause into your semester schedule, then use the gathering to speak with someone outside your usual classes or organization.
cards.short_summary: Students, faculty and staff gather weekly for conversation and a morning snack.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon identifies College Coffee as a weekly community event begun in 1984 and held during fall and spring undergraduate semesters on Tuesday mornings.
cards.source_title: Events & Activities | Elon Traditions | Elon University
cards.access_notes: The traditions page lists Tuesdays from 9:40 to 10:20 a.m. during fall and spring undergraduate semesters; verify the current venue before attending.

cards.title: Pause for Numen Lumen on Thursday
cards.subtitle: Elon’s motto becomes a recurring space for reflection and expression
cards.notes: Attend with an open mind, listen to the featured community story or performance, and leave room for viewpoints different from your own.
cards.short_summary: A weekly gathering joins personal reflection with stories, music and artistic expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon describes Numen Lumen as one of its oldest student traditions and a weekly Thursday opportunity for reflection on mind, body and spirit.
cards.source_title: Events & Activities | Elon Traditions | Elon University
cards.access_notes: The university identifies it as a Thursday tradition; consult the current university events calendar for the speaker, venue and session status.

cards.title: Sign the Honor Code Together
cards.subtitle: New students publicly affirm four shared values each fall
cards.notes: Read the Honor Code before the ceremony, listen to the campus speakers, and treat your signature as a commitment beyond the event itself.
cards.short_summary: New students recite a pledge and sign an Honor Code display centered on four core values.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon says Call to Honor occurs each fall, when new students learn about honesty, integrity, responsibility and respect, recite the pledge and sign the Honor Code.
cards.access_notes: This fall event is designed for new students; ceremony details are communicated through university orientation channels.

cards.title: Follow the Luminary-Lined Paths
cards.subtitle: Thousands of lights turn central campus into a multifaith learning walk
cards.notes: Walk the illuminated campus route, stop at educational stations, and engage respectfully with the religious and cultural traditions represented.
cards.short_summary: An annual evening combines illuminated pathways, learning stations, performances and community reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon documents the Festival of Lights and Luminaries as an annual campus tradition featuring thousands of luminaries and educational stations about religious, spiritual, ethical and cultural traditions.
cards.source_title: Elon to celebrate ‘many lights on one night’ at Festival of Lights and Luminaries
cards.access_notes: The festival is held annually, but dates and weather plans change; use the current Truitt Center or university event announcement.

cards.title: Let Faculty Serve the Finals Breakfast
cards.subtitle: The people assigning exams switch roles before finals week
cards.notes: Watch Student Union Board announcements near finals, arrive within the posted service window, and use the break to reset before studying.
cards.short_summary: Faculty and staff serve a late-night breakfast-style meal to students around finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon describes Cram Jam as a before-finals tradition in which faculty and staff serve students late-night pancakes, bacon, eggs and potatoes at Lakeside Dining Hall.
cards.source_title: Events & Activities | Elon Traditions | Elon University
cards.access_notes: Held around finals with event-specific timing; confirm the current Student Union Board announcement and any student-access requirements.

cards.title: Wave a White Towel for Dr. D
cards.subtitle: A basketball exchange became a continuing tribute to a former Elon president
cards.notes: Bring or accept a white rally towel at an appropriate athletics event, then learn why the gesture honors J. Earl “Dr. D” Danieley.
cards.short_summary: Fans continue a white-towel gesture begun by former president and devoted basketball supporter J. Earl Danieley.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon says the rally-towel tradition began after students chanted for J. Earl Danieley at basketball games and he responded by waving a white towel; fans continue the gesture in his memory.
cards.source_title: Symbols & Sayings | Elon Traditions | Elon University
cards.access_notes: The university says towels are waved at many athletic competitions; game admission and towel availability depend on the specific event.

cards.title: Sing the Alma Mater’s Unusual First Line
cards.subtitle: The 1998 song explicitly remembers Elon’s coeducational founding
cards.notes: Read the university’s explanation of the lyrics, then join the song at a formal ceremony, major event or athletics contest when invited.
cards.short_summary: A campus song links Elon’s oaks, hilltop setting and coeducational history to communal ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon states that students and alumni have sung the Alma Mater at formal ceremonies, athletic contests and major events since it was written in 1998.
cards.source_title: The Alma Mater | Elon Traditions | Elon University
cards.access_notes: Participation occurs when the Alma Mater is included in a ceremony, major event or athletic contest; access follows the host event’s rules.

cards.title: Take the President’s Holiday-Party Photo
cards.subtitle: A late-1980s presidential reception evolved into a student celebration
cards.notes: Check the December invitation, enjoy the student performances, and use the themed photo setup for a lighthearted record of the semester.
cards.short_summary: Students gather for a presidential holiday reception featuring food, music and themed photographs.
cards.evidence_claim: Elon says the President’s Holiday Party for Students began in the late 1980s at Maynard House and now includes food, student musicians and photographs with the university president.
cards.source_title: Events & Activities | Elon Traditions | Elon University
cards.access_notes: The university lists this student tradition in December; verify the current invitation, venue and eligibility through campus communications.
